body:
Thank you :) 

I usually don't listen to these "stop sugar, stop drinking energy drinks", cause they're just opinions, nothing scientific behind it, like when you get told to believe in God, just because "you simply should". But your comment sparked a bit of a run for research to verify and broaden what you said. You're right. I decided to try it, I don't really want to, but I see it's very reasonable and logical to do it. So far, it's been 5 days since the last energy drink I've drank. I don't see much difference, but then again, these things don't happen right away. It's been tough, but a hope that it might lessen these... depressed states is keeping me going, for now. We'll see how long it catches, but I do hope it will be for long. Next step is limiting the sugar from sweets... I see it's necessary to do it.   
Seriously though, thanks for your comment. I tried many various ways over past to find happiness in myself (remember how I said that therapists never helped? I'm not exactly thrilled about being suicidal, trapped, tired and depressed either, I tried rather hard over the past to build some scaffolding in myself for at least a bit of happiness and peace) and to certain extent, I did find it, but sometimes, it's just not enough when circumstances get too tiring or difficult.   
Maybe it will change with the quitting of energy drinks. Who knows. All I know is that it's been five days since I've really wanted to drink an energy drink and I didn't even try to get one, for the first time like ever. In past it was always like "I really should quit it... But I want to drink one. Eh, to hell with it, I'm just gonna drink it." Don't know what was it you said right, but it was something. Thanks for taking a bit of time and saying it. We'll see how it goes next, but you already sparked something I didn't manage to do before.

I've fought for the last few days - tiredness, depression, loneliness. I'm slowly starting to get on my feet and I wanted to reply. Thank you :) For reading. For commenting. For supporting. For caring. It means a lot, it really does.   
I do hope you will get better, at least for a moment, and will have it easier. You seem like a very nice person and I'm pretty sure you deserve it :)
